reason: JSON.parse coerces via toString(), which defaults to utf8 for a Buffer, so parsing succeeds identically either way

content: Stryker disable next-line MethodExpression -- proven killed under direct vitest execution but Stryker's own coverage attribution never runs the two tests that would kill it; see the comment above.
justification: This mutant (replacing `[...].filter(Boolean).join(" — ")` with the bare array `[...]`) is a real behavioral change that a correct test suite should kill, and it is killed -- just not by Stryker's own instrumented run. Verified directly: applying this exact replacement to the source file by hand and running `npx vitest run test/unit/presets/shared/vitest-json-policy.test.ts` (no Stryker involved) fails 4 of that file's 11 tests, including the two that assert the complete rationale string via `toBe(...)` rather than `toContain(...)` specifically to make this class of mutation observable. Under `npx stryker run` -- reproduced across three separate invocations (scoped to this file plus missing-dependency.ts, twice; the full, unscoped project run once) -- this mutant's own `coveredBy`/`testsCompleted` fields show only 6 of the file's 11 tests ever executed against it, and none of those 6 are the two `toBe` tests that would catch it. `stryker.config.mjs`'s own comment already documents choosing `coverageAnalysis: "all"` specifically because `"perTest"` exhibited "coverage-attribution quirks (a mutant on a line every throwing-policy test genuinely exercises was reported as only covered by unrelated tests)" during this repository's own implementation -- this is the same class of quirk surfacing under `"all"` as well, for this one line.
alternatives: Rewrite the source to avoid the exact `array.filter(Boolean).join(sep)` chain shape (e.g. building the string with an imperative loop instead) purely to dodge whatever makes Stryker misattribute coverage for it -- rejected: it would make the code worse to read for a tooling quirk, and there is no evidence a differently-shaped equivalent wouldn't hit the same or a different attribution gap. Switching `coverageAnalysis` to `"off"` (no coverage-based filtering at all, for every mutant in the whole project) would also fix this specific case, but at a real, whole-project performance cost to fix one file's one mutant.
remediation: Not pursued: no test-suite change closes this gap, since the existing tests already kill the mutation under real execution -- the gap is entirely in Stryker's own per-mutant test-selection bookkeeping for this line, which this repository does not control. Re-check whether a future `@stryker-mutator/core`/`@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` upgrade resolves the attribution gap before assuming it is permanent.
reason: proven killed under direct vitest execution but Stryker's own coverage attribution never runs the two tests that would kill it; see the comment above.

remediation: The reference is never called here -- it's saved and later reassigned back onto `AbortSignal.any` to restore it, so a wrapping arrow function would add indirection purely to satisfy a rule about call-time `this` binding that this code path never exercises.
